This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Tango (habanera)**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

A held chord on 1, then short ones on the and of 2, on 3 and on 4.

It belongs in *Tango*. Here it is in the tango style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tango"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Quarter-note chords

Start with something simpler. The chord on every beat, held. On the piano the left hand adds the root underneath as each chord arrives: Let It Be, Imagine, Someone Like You.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-quarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="72" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Quarter-note chords","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Tango (habanera), slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A held chord on 1, then short marked ones on the and of 2, on 3 and on 4. Play it with weight and clear separation.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="72" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tango"}},{"label":"Quarter-note chords (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"quarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 104 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tango"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am|Am|E7|Am" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tango"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="tango" data-chart="Am Dm|E7 Am|Dm E7|Am" data-tempo="104" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Tango (habanera)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tango"}}]'></div>
